title: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
mutable_substrate: The production agent system's full source-level substrate, including skills, prompts, memory, workflows, and harness code for routing, hooks, dispatch, mediation, state, and lifecycle.
optimization_operator: A pluggable external coding-agent CLI performs stage-scoped source edits; MOSS deterministically sequences Locate, Plan, Plan-Review, Implement, Code-Review, Task-Evaluate, and Verdict, with bounded review-revision loops.
feedback_selection: Directed batches are built from automatically scored production-session chunks and explicit user flags. Candidate images replay the same batch in ephemeral containers; qualitative strong/adequate/weak/missing keypoint matrices drive four-way verdicts and plateau stopping.
archive_memory: Artifacts include production transcripts, a locked baseline keypoint matrix, cross-iteration matrices, plans, diffs, commits, build logs, and trial outputs. Evolution follows one bounded candidate line rather than a population archive; a last-known-good image supports rollback.
validation_strategy: Runtime replay of every batch task for multiple trials in isolated containers built from the exact candidate image, followed by user-consent-gated promotion and liveness health probes. The case study reuses the optimization batch for evaluation and has no held-out regression suite.
adaptation_mode: Post-deployment, batch-triggered offline evolution with an online conversational control surface and state-preserving in-place release; it is not per-request runtime rewriting.
principal_results: A single OpenClaw evolution cycle with DeepSeek V3.2 changes three harness files with 177 insertions and one deletion, adding a tool-result annotation branch, a pre-call deny gate, helpers, and tests.

Across four tasks and three trials per task, the mean claweval score rises from 0.2526 to 0.6100 (+0.3574, approximately +141.5% relative), although the final mean remains below the 0.75 pass threshold.
All three T138 trials exceed the 0.75 pass threshold; only one of three T137zh trials passes, and SLA arithmetic and tier classification remain unresolved.
The same four tasks form both the evolution batch and post-swap evaluation, so the evidence establishes targeted within-batch repair rather than held-out generalization.
The source-level claim is directly supported by the case patch's changes to mediator and before-tool-call harness logic rather than prompts, skills, memory, or workflow configuration.
limitations: One substrate, one base model, one batch, one iteration, four tasks, and three trials per task provide no statistical or longitudinal reliability evidence.
The optimization batch is also the test set; there is no held-out task set or unrelated regression suite.
No ablation or matched comparison tests whether text-only, hybrid, or human repair could achieve the same result.
Exact depth budgets, iteration limits, review rounds, trial counts, plateau thresholds, coding-agent provider used in the case, token cost, build time, and wall-clock duration are not reported.
The claims of deterministic effect and immunity to long-context drift are conceptual and not directly evaluated.
Trial workers omit live user state and production traffic, while health probes check liveness rather than semantic behavior.
The case auto-acknowledges user consent and does not exercise user review, rollback, or a failed deployment.
The same Task-Evaluate mechanism helps curate evidence, defines keypoints, evaluates candidates, and informs verdicts, creating correlated blind spots.
No multi-user privacy, persistent-state schema compatibility, or irreversible external-side-effect analysis is provided.
safety_controls: Directed failure batches constrain proposal intent instead of open-ended mutation.
Plan-Review and Code-Review are bounded gates; rejected code rounds hard-reset the working tree.
Candidate images are replayed in short-lived workers isolated from the live container's network and state mounts.
Promotion pauses for an explicit user-issued apply command in normal operation.
The swap uses an atomic request file, a 90-second probe window sampled every 5 seconds, four liveness checks, and three consecutive passes.
Rollback uses an independently stored last-known-good image, and user state remains in a host-mounted volume.
The paper does not specify sandboxing, least privilege, code signing, dependency controls, security analysis, secret isolation, state snapshots, or recovery from irreversible external side effects.

explicit_predecessors.name: SICA
explicit_predecessors.evidence: MOSS cites SICA as demonstrating that an agent can edit its implementation and improve SWE-bench performance on a minimal scaffold.

explicit_predecessors.name: Darwin Gödel Machine
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper cites archive-based open-ended source evolution, then replaces benchmark fitness and population search with a bounded failure-directed production loop.

explicit_predecessors.name: HyperAgents
explicit_predecessors.evidence: HyperAgents is cited for extending editability to the meta-procedure; MOSS instead keeps its orchestrator's stage ordering and verdicts deterministic.

explicit_predecessors.name: Meta-Harness
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper names Meta-Harness's result that execution traces improve proposal quality beyond benchmark-score feedback, aligning with MOSS's production-transcript evidence.

explicit_predecessors.name: Hermes Agent
explicit_predecessors.evidence: MOSS's comparison table marks Hermes as evolving skills and memory but not prompts or harness code.

explicit_predecessors.name: SkillClaw, GenericAgent, Capability Evolver, and EvoAgentX
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper assigns these systems to skills, memory, behavioral genes, SOPs, prompts, or workflow graphs and claims none edits the harness.

explicit_predecessors.name: DSPy and GEPA
explicit_predecessors.evidence: These optimizers are cited as compiling or searching prompts associated with application-level agents, a design space MOSS treats as a subset of source-level editing.

explicit_predecessors.name: OpenClaw
explicit_predecessors.evidence: MOSS is implemented and evaluated by rewriting OpenClaw's mediator and hook-chain source while preserving its deployed user-state volume.

open_questions: Does source-level repair outperform prompt, skill, hybrid, and human repair under matched incidents, costs, and regression suites?
How well do batch-targeted patches generalize to held-out related tasks while preserving unrelated behavior?
What sandbox, permission, signing, dependency, secret, and human-review controls make generated source edits safe enough for production?
How can rollback compensate for remote side effects or persistent-state corruption that image restoration cannot undo?
Are automatic evidence curation and four-level keypoint judgments calibrated against users and hard checks?
Can model-limit and architecture-limit verdicts be validated against ground truth?
How do proposer provider, depth, iteration budget, and trial count affect repair rate, regressions, cost, and latency?
Do source fixes actually remain stable longer than equivalent prompt or memory fixes under accumulating context and patches?
Can safe canaries or shadow traffic test candidate images with realistic state without exposing production data?
How should session evidence be consented, redacted, retained, tenant-isolated, and deleted?
